subject: Discovery recap + scheduling dedicated capacity sizing call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@fintechco.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps (dedicated capacity sizing call)

Hi Asha — great to meet today, and thanks for the clear context on FinTechCo's roadmap. Quick recap from our side:

- Primary use cases: real-time customer support triage (text), automated document summarization for compliance reviews, and fraud detection enrichment (low-latency scoring).
- Expected steady-state usage: ~12K requests/day, median payload ~350 tokens, peak window ~1200 reqs/min during business hours.
- Latency target: 95th < 300ms, 99th preferably < 500ms for single-turn scoring.

Next step: Camila (cc'd) — our Solutions Engineer — will lead a dedicated capacity sizing call to map those throughput/latency targets to dedicated capacity (GPU sizing, batching, and KV cache strategy).

Can you confirm which of these windows works for your team next week (all times PT):
- Tue 2027-05-11, 10:00–11:00
- Tue 2027-05-11, 14:00–15:00
- Wed 2027-05-12, 09:00–10:00

Attached a short pre-call questionnaire (pre-call-questionnaire.xlsx) — filling it out will help Camila size things more accurately. I've also attached a preliminary pricing estimate for the usage you shared.

Agenda suggestion for the sizing call:
1) Quick recap of workloads & SLA targets
2) Traffic profile and peak patterns (you)
3) Model selection and quantization options (us)
4) Autoscaling/burst policy and fallback plan (us)
5) Action items and proposed Dedicated config

If those windows don't work, let us know 2–3 alternatives and we'll align.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa

From: Asha Menon <asha@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (dedicated capacity sizing call)

Marissa — thanks for the summary and for the docs. Sounds good to us; Camila, glad to meet you. A couple quick clarifications before the sizing call so we can come prepared:

- Confirming the peak: the 1200 reqs/min is for the ticketing flow (text scoring). We also have a batch job that runs nightly (~200K docs) but that's lower priority for the sizing call — mostly off-peak.
- Models: we'll likely evaluate a 7B/13B family for real-time scoring; can you size both options?
- Latency: 99th < 500ms is our hard requirement for scoring; for the support triage path 95th < 250ms would be ideal.

For availability, Wed 2027-05-12 09:00–10:00 PT works best for our engineering leads (I'll invite Anil from infra); Tue afternoon is tight for us.

I'll fill out the questionnaire and drop it in the Drive link. Looking forward to the call.

—Asha

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (dedicated capacity sizing call)

Thanks Asha — Wed 05/12 09:00 PT is on my calendar. Quick note on what we'll want to cover and what would help make the call efficient:

Pre-call asks (if possible):
- Sample QPS distribution (5m granularity) for the last 2 weeks (or a typical week).
- A few representative payloads (anonymized) for the scoring flow and support triage (so we can estimate tokenization and KV cache hit behavior).
- Any constraints on model selection (e.g., must be open-weight models vs. ok to use Redwood-curated variants).

On the call we'll:
- Walk through spike estimates for both 7B and 13B variants, including: GPU type assumptions, expected batching gains, and 95/99 percentile latency estimates under steady-state and burst.
- Recommend a Dedicated config (pool size, autoscale thresholds, burst capacity, and fallback model routing).
- Highlight key telemetry we will want to capture post-deploy to validate SLOs.

I've attached our pre-call questionnaire to this thread (pre-call-questionnaire.xlsx) and a short template for sample payloads. If you can drop the stats/payloads in the Drive link Marissa shared, we'll be able to run a tighter sizing exercise during the call.

See you Wed — Camila
